design_note: The earlier labs address lost entitlement and modified proposals. This matrix makes the independence requirement concrete: two decision events can represent only one person, or include the requester. It separates distinct identities, present entitlement and separation of duties without presenting a universal approval count.

source.title: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations
source.concept: Control AC-5 calls for identifying duties that require separation and defining access authorizations that support that separation. Organizations define the duties and associated policy.
source.scope: The two-approver refund rule and people are fictional. NIST does not prescribe this example threshold, and passing these identity checks alone does not permit execution.

lesson.title: Two approval events may still be one approver
lesson.intro: Priya requested refund P-77. This fictional rule requires two distinct, currently entitled approvers, neither of whom is Priya. Each row contains two authenticated approval events for that exact proposal.

data.rule: All columns must allow; binding, expiry and current resource conditions still apply.

read: The columns test three separate conditions on the same pair of decisions.
Mira signing twice does not create a second independent principal.
Priya is entitled generally but cannot independently approve her own request here.
lesson.question: Do two valid signatures by Mira satisfy the stated rule?
lesson.answer: No. Signature validity establishes the source of each decision, not distinct reviewers. Both events resolve to Mira, so the pair lacks a second principal. A currently entitled, independent second approver is required, along with the remaining execution checks.
lesson.takeaway: Count distinct entitled principals, not clicks or signatures.
lesson.assumption: Fictional two-person rule; all decisions are approved, correctly bound and unexpired. The ex-member has no current approval role.
